title: Event listeners
learningObjectives: Explain event listeners and update browser documents with safe DOM and event patterns.

understand.concept: Event listeners register functions that run when an event occurs. addEventListener() accepts an event type and callback, with optional settings such as once, capture, and passive. removeEventListener() can remove a listener when the same callback reference and matching options are supplied.
understand.whyItMatters: Event-driven code powers buttons, forms, keyboard interaction, and browser behaviour. Keep handlers focused, avoid duplicate registrations, and clean up listeners when components are removed or reinitialised.
understand.analogy: An event listener is a doorbell: when the event happens, the registered callback is called.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual DOM, event, and security behaviour follows browser platform rules.

explain.narrative: The click event invokes the greet callback and updates the output text.

examples.explanation: The click event invokes the greet callback and updates the output text.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser page updates in response to safe DOM operations or user events.

practise.guidedTask: Add click and input listeners to a small page. Remove one listener using the same function reference and explain why an inline anonymous function is harder to remove.
practise.independentTask: Build a small interactive component using DOM methods and event listeners. Handle missing elements and user input safely.
hints: Keep event handlers focused and avoid duplicate listeners.
Use event delegation for suitable dynamic lists.

questions.prompt: Which method registers an event listener on an element?
questions.explanation: addEventListener() registers an event handler for the specified event type.

questions.prompt: What is a safe DOM update pattern for user-provided text?
options: Set textContent on an existing element
Build an HTML string and assign it to innerHTML
questions.answer: Set textContent on an existing element
questions.explanation: textContent treats the value as text and avoids parsing untrusted markup.
